name: Acropolis & Parthenon
note: Go at opening time or late afternoon to dodge crowds and heat.

name: Acropolis Museum
note: Glass floors over excavations; cafe terrace faces the Parthenon.

name: Ancient Agora & Temple of Hephaestus
note: Best-preserved Greek temple; quieter than the Acropolis.

name: Anafiotika
note: Tiny whitewashed island-style lanes under the Acropolis.

name: Monastiraki Square & Flea Market
note: Flea market streets; busiest on Sundays.

name: National Archaeological Museum
note: Mask of Agamemnon and the Antikythera mechanism.

name: Lycabettus Hill
note: Highest point in the centre; go for sunset (funicular or walk).

name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
note: Huge columns next to Hadrian's Arch.

name: Panathenaic Stadium
note: All-marble stadium of the first modern Olympics.

name: Philopappos Hill
note: Free, shaded walk with the best Acropolis view.

name: Areopagus Hill
note: Rocky outcrop by the Acropolis entrance; sunset spot.

name: Varvakios Central Market
note: Meat, fish and spice market; go in the morning.

name: National Garden
note: Shady escape behind Parliament.

name: Stavros Niarchos Cultural Center
note: Renzo Piano building, park and sea views.

name: Museum of Cycladic Art
note: Minimalist Cycladic figurines.

name: Psyrri
note: Street art, tavernas and bars; lively at night.

name: Kerameikos
note: Ancient cemetery; calm and rarely crowded.

name: Roman Agora & Tower of the Winds
note: Small site, included in the combined ticket.

name: Plaka
note: Old town lanes; touristy but lovely early morning.

name: Koukaki
note: Local cafes and bars south of the Acropolis.

name: Syntagma Square – Changing of the Guard
note: Evzones change every hour; big ceremony Sundays 11:00.

name: Benaki Museum
note: Greek culture from antiquity to today; rooftop cafe.

name: Kolonaki
note: Upscale shopping, galleries and cafes.
